corrections.claim: Show RoCoF, not just frequency
corrections.page: ERCOT publishes frequency every 10 s. A 10-s slope understates a trip's first-second RoCoF by roughly 7-22x, so the page shows expected RoCoF from inertia instead.

corrections.claim: Show time error
corrections.page: ERCOT still corrects time error at +/-30 s (NOG 2.2.9.1); NERC BAL-004-0 is retired. It is clock-keeping, not stability: today it moved about 2.5 s.

corrections.claim: PRC is the reserve that can arrest a fall
corrections.page: PRC counts MW, not speed. Whether a fall stops depends on PRC and inertia together; governor/PFR headroom, FFR and load relays do the arresting.

corrections.claim: Frequency lags; inertia + RoCoF lead
corrections.page: Measured RoCoF only exists after an event starts. The leading pair is inertia + PRC (and the largest contingency).

corrections.claim: Design trip 2,750 MW
corrections.page: 2,750 MW (2018 paper); ERCOT's 2024 AS Study uses 2,800 MW. Both shown.

corrections.claim: The ramp strands an operator balanced a minute ago
corrections.page: SCED re-dispatches every ~5 min, so a forecast ramp gets scheduled. What strands an operator is ramp forecast error: on 25 Sep the day-ahead plan missed 2,624 MW of the HE16-HE18 rise.

corrections.claim: Net load (actual and forecast) is ERCOT data
corrections.page: ERCOT publishes the parts; net load = demand - wind - solar is our arithmetic on curtailed actuals.

corrections.claim: A home-battery fleet can offer all five reserve products
corrections.page: ADERs may offer ECRS and Non-Spin only (RRS only with PFR under a cap; no Regulation). Reg and RRS numbers are reference only.

corrections.claim: Procured and physically available reserve can both be shown
corrections.page: ERCOT's "capability" is at most the award, so it never shows spare. PRC and the "any combination" row are gross, including awarded AS.

corrections.claim: Reserve behind a transmission constraint is not reserve
corrections.page: ERCOT derates such reserve by hand before awarding (the public awards are already net of it). For ADERs it does not enforce distribution limits at all: that job is Base's.

corrections.claim: ECRS-backed and Non-Spin-backed kW can be held together
corrections.page: They are alternatives from the same stored energy: ECRS alone OR Non-Spin alone, or a mix on one line.

corrections.claim: MW on every element vs its thermal rating
corrections.page: Ratings are amps or MVA. We compare current (lines) and kVA (transformers).

corrections.claim: ERCOT has five DC ties
corrections.page: Four in service (East 600, North 220, Railroad 300, Laredo VFT 100 MW). Eagle Pass (36 MW) has been out since 2020; the RTSC page still lists it at 0 MW.

corrections.claim: A grid can be at 60 Hz and collapsing in voltage in one corner
corrections.page: ERCOT prices voltage-stability limits (EASTEX bound 175 of 279 SCED runs). Our feeder shows a sag toward the ANSI floor, not a collapse, and has no frequency of its own.

corrections.claim: ERCOT publishes bus voltages / MVAr (implicit)
corrections.page: Not publicly: voltage profiles and GTC definitions need a certificate. The public trace of a voltage limit is a shadow price.

corrections.claim: Use the IEEE 1547-2018 default volt-var
corrections.page: The Cat B default curve exists, but the default mode is unity PF unless the utility enables volt-var. Oncor's setting is UNVERIFIED.

corrections.claim: RTCA runs continuously
corrections.page: It runs periodically (about every 5 min per a 2012 ERCOT paper; current cadence UNVERIFIED).

corrections.claim: RTCA outputs the binding constraints with shadow prices
corrections.page: Contingency analysis finds the violations; SCED prices them. The public list (NP6-86-CD) also carries non-binding rows.

corrections.claim: N-1 on a feeder works like N-1 on the grid
corrections.page: A radial feeder does not shift flow; it interrupts. Feeder N-1 is a restoration question. Our extract has no tie switches, so "dark" means dark until repair here.

corrections.claim: A stale measurement produces confident wrong answers
corrections.page: Where a meter exists the error shows up as a residual. It is confidently wrong only where nothing measures (in 2003 the estimator failed loudly; the alarm system failed silently).

corrections.claim: "mw:Provenance" discipline
corrections.page: The term appears nowhere; the page uses CIM MeasurementValueQuality (validity + oldData) and the dossier's provenance chips.

openIssues.text: Replays run every Core at OpenDSS default PF 0.88 (volt found it). flow, res, n1, dq and load reproduce the replays and inherit it. synth pfcheck quantifies the numbers the console quotes. Real fix: set kvar after kW in sim/feeder.py battery(), rebuild replays, rerun the six item builds.

Upward reserve: the "voltage band binds" result (ECRS alone 1,270.4 idle / 938.4 co-opt) does not hold at unity PF, where the energy cap binds (1,439.0 / 1,063.3 kW; max home 1.0487 pu, max line 85.5% / 81.6%). The "uniform-cut collapse" rests on a 25 kVA transformer at 99.5% that is 83.8% at unity.
Downward 4.7 kW rests on pad switch 258965 (115 A), a rating item flow shows the dataset contradicts. Lead with the head-bound figure (175 kW at 19:45, res sensitivity).

12 minor review fixes are not applied in freq-series.json / freq-spec.md (wedge is an estimate not a bound; trip slope 0.026-0.082 Hz/s = 7-22x; FME range 510-1,323 MW; per-array status; inertia update wording; "none found" wording; instantaneous per RTSC help; 3,200 MW tagged pre-RTC+B; RRS-PFR/governor; 1547 DER deadband 0.036 Hz). The console uses the corrected wording.
